That pattern usually means the CSRF token is no longer being sent with the request. If the token only lived in a form field or template block that stayed in the base template, the partial's form posts without it, so Django returns 403. I haven't seen your files, so this is the likely cause rather than a confirmed one. Fixes are to put `{% csrf_token %}` inside the form in the partial, or send the token in an hx-headers X-CSRFToken header on a parent element.
Action: Look at the partial and the base template to see where the token is rendered and how hx-post is configured, then fix it; if you paste the partial and the base template body tag I can confirm.

A common cause is that the partial is rendered or swapped without the token: the base template's token only helps if the form is inside it or htmx sends it as a header. Two fixes: put `{% csrf_token %}` inside the form in the partial, or set `hx-headers='{"X-CSRFToken": "{{ csrf_token }}"}'` on the body so every hx-post carries it. Also check the view renders the partial with request context.
Action: look at the partial and the view to see which of these applies.

A Django CSRF 403 on `hx-post` after moving a form into a partial usually means the request no longer carries the token: the partial has no `{% csrf_token %}`, or the token is sent via `hx-headers` (`X-CSRFToken`) on an element that isn't an ancestor of the form anymore, or the partial is rendered without the request so no token is available. Having it in the base template only helps if the form actually inherits it. Action: look at the partial and base template to see how the token is supplied and how the view renders the partial, then fix that one spot.

htmx doesn't add the CSRF token on its own; Django needs it as a header or hidden input. Likely causes after moving to a partial: the token was supplied by an attribute that no longer applies (like `hx-headers` on `<body>`), or the partial is rendered without the request so `csrf_token` is empty.
Action: show me the base template, the partial and the view, and check in the network tab whether the request carries `X-CSRFToken` or a `csrfmiddlewaretoken` field.
